source.title: Selective erasure of a fear memory

confidence_rationale: Ablating the sparse LA neurons allocated to a fear memory (high-CREB) after learning erases that memory, while ablating a matched random fraction does not. Supports MECH-599's claim that a conditioned threat prediction lives in a discrete, removable, cue-specific structure. Also disconfirming-direction for the MECH-598 dependency: allocation here is by neuronal excitability, not by surprise-driven associability.
failure_signatures: A specific fear memory is held by a sparse, identifiable neuronal subpopulation whose removal erases it; a purely contextual, distributed harm field (residue / harm_eval) would not show this selective erasure.

Which neurons join the memory trace is set by CREB-linked excitability at encoding, not by surprise-driven associability -- cue-specific threat memory can form without the MECH-598 mechanism, which weakens MECH-599's depends_on edge to MECH-598.

mapping.source_claim_statement: LA neurons with increased CREB are preferentially recruited into a fear memory trace; selectively ablating them after learning (but not a similar portion of random LA neurons) robustly and persistently blocks expression of that fear memory.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports the existence of a discrete, cue-specific threat store as distinct from REE's contextual threat machinery -- the same kind of object SD-051 is on the safety side. It also bears on MECH-599's dependency on MECH-598: in biology a cue-specific threat store forms under a competition-by-excitability allocation rule, with no associability state required.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Tests a single conditioned memory (tone-shock) and shows removal, not cue competition among candidates. Allocation-by-excitability is a different credit rule from MECH-598's; it does not refute associability, but it shows cue specificity does not need it.
mapping.source_context: Mouse; CREB overexpression in LA with inducible diphtheria-toxin ablation after auditory fear conditioning

confidence_components.notes: Science, clean control (random-ablation arm). Mapping moderate: discrete store supported; the credit rule differs from REE's proposal.
